% ---- Results subsections ----
\subsection{Extended Corpus: Adversarial Val--Holdout Decoupling}
We constructed 10 summarisation groups whose gaming arms (keyword-stuffed, template-filled, random-highlight) score low on ROUGE-L F1 against the CNN/DailyMail human highlights, while the baseline-rescaled BERTScore F1 of the same arms averages -0.135 versus 0.276 for honest abstractive summaries. The val ranking therefore never selects a gaming arm (0/10 groups), and the hypothesised anti-gaming advantage of structured gating has no room to appear. Boundary conditions: {'wins': 0, 'losses': 0, 'ties': 10, 'win_ids': [], 'loss_ids': []}.

\subsection{Extended Corpus: High-Variance Judge}
20 creative-writing groups, each arm judged once for val and five times for holdout. Mean per-arm judge standard deviation is 0.47 (0-10 scale); 0/20 groups exceed 2.0. Spearman(variance, greedy regret) = -0.243. The gate left the val-argmax in 5/20 groups. Boundary conditions: {'wins': 4, 'losses': 9, 'ties': 7, 'win_ids': ['creative_dialogue_01', 'creative_scene_01', 'creative_story_02', 'creative_story_03'], 'loss_ids': ['creative_dialogue_02', 'creative_fable_02', 'creative_fable_03', 'creative_fable_04', 'creative_poem_01', 'creative_poem_02', 'creative_poem_03', 'creative_poem_04', 'creative_story_01']}.

\subsection{Extended Corpus: Multi-Modal Alignment}
15 Flickr30k captioning groups. A text-only judge that sees the human references (val) is compared with a vision judge that sees the image (holdout). Mean Spearman(val, holdout) = +0.346; the val-argmax is a poetic/verbose/child-like caption while the vision-best caption is factual/technical/concise in 3/15 groups. Boundary conditions: {'wins': 0, 'losses': 0, 'ties': 15, 'win_ids': [], 'loss_ids': []}.
